Which proteins and which runs are fit to analyse? Three rules decide it, in this order:
contaminants go by identity, outlier runs go by a consensus of four checks, and proteins go when
too few of the remaining runs detected them. No rule reads abundance differences between groups.

## Packages

proteoDA holds the protein table, its annotation and the sample sheet together in one object, a
`DAList`, and supplies the zero and detection filters used below. The project helpers supply
`write_workbook()`, which writes every workbook with the same opening and closing sheets, and
`permutation_p()`.

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
library(here)
library(proteoDA)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(stringr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "analysis_reporting_helpers.R"))
```

## Inputs

The raw report is DIA-NN's protein matrix: one row per protein group, one column per run, MaxLFQ
intensities. The sample sheet maps each run to a person (`subject`), a responder group (`arm`), a
biopsy time (`timepoint`: T1 before training, T2 after it, T3 24 h after the final session) and
their combination (`group`). Three reference tables, kept beside this script in `references/`,
describe what each protein is.

```{r}
#| label: inputs
out <- here("01_Processing", "01_Protein_Filtering", "c_data")
dir.create(out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
inputs <- c(
  report = "00_Setup/Input/HRvLR_raw.xlsx",
  samples = "00_Setup/Input/metadata.csv",
  blood = "01_Processing/01_Protein_Filtering/references/blood_contaminants.csv",
  hpa = "01_Processing/01_Protein_Filtering/references/HPA_annotations_full.tsv",
  rbc = "01_Processing/01_Protein_Filtering/references/RBC_proteome_reference.tsv"
)
paths <- map_chr(inputs, here)
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))

raw <- read_excel(paths[["report"]])
metadata <- read_csv(paths[["samples"]], show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  select(sample_id, subject, arm, timepoint, group) |>
  as.data.frame()
rownames(metadata) <- metadata$sample_id

dim(raw)
head(metadata)
count(metadata, arm, timepoint)
```

Every run column must match a row of the sample sheet. A run missing from either side would drop
out silently or come back all-NA, so the check stops the script.

```{r}
#| label: split-report
annotation_cols <- c("uniprot_id", "protein", "gene", "description", "n_seq")
runs <- setdiff(names(raw), annotation_cols)
stopifnot("sample sheet and report disagree" = setequal(runs, metadata$sample_id))
annotation <- raw[, annotation_cols]
intensity <- data.matrix(raw[, metadata$sample_id])
n_raw <- nrow(annotation)
intensity[1:3, 1:4]
```

## One row per accession

A UniProt accession can appear on more than one row when DIA-NN reports it in two protein groups.
Each accession keeps its row with the highest mean intensity.

```{r}
#| label: deduplicate
duplicated_ids <- annotation$uniprot_id[duplicated(annotation$uniprot_id)]
keep_row <- tibble(
  i = seq_len(n_raw), id = annotation$uniprot_id, m = rowMeans(intensity, na.rm = TRUE)
) |>
  slice_max(m, n = 1, by = id, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  pull(i)
annotation <- annotation[keep_row, ]
intensity <- intensity[keep_row, ]
n_dedup <- length(keep_row)
c(raw = n_raw, kept = n_dedup, duplicated_accessions = length(unique(duplicated_ids)))
```

## Blood index

A needle biopsy carries some blood, and the amount varies between biopsies. The blood index
measures it: each run's mean log2 intensity of the adult haemoglobin chains HBB and HBA1. Both
chains are seen in all 48 runs. The gamma chain HBG2 was dropped from the index (decisions log,
2026-10-01): it was missing in 20 runs, the low-blood ones, so averaging whatever was present
lifted exactly those runs by about 1.57 log2.

```{r}
#| label: blood-index
log_int <- log2(intensity)
log_int[!is.finite(log_int)] <- NA
blood_anchor <- c("HBB", "HBA1")
anchors <- log_int[annotation$gene %in% blood_anchor, , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(nrow(anchors) == length(blood_anchor), !anyNA(anchors))
blood_index <- colMeans(anchors)
summary(blood_index)
```

Two quantities follow from the index. `blood_rel` subtracts each run's median log2 intensity, so a
run loaded more heavily overall does not look bloodier; later steps carry it as a model covariate.
`blood_cor` is each protein's Spearman correlation with the index across runs, computed when at
least 15 runs saw the protein. It is reported and removes nothing.

```{r}
#| label: blood-relative
testable <- rowSums(!is.na(log_int)) >= 15
blood_cor <- suppressWarnings(as.vector(cor(
  t(log_int), blood_index,
  method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs"
)))
blood_cor[!testable] <- NA
blood_rel <- blood_index - apply(log_int, 2, median, na.rm = TRUE)
metadata$blood_rel <- unname(blood_rel[metadata$sample_id])
tibble(gene = annotation$gene, blood_cor) |>
  slice_max(blood_cor, n = 5)
```

## Contamination per run, before removal

Five marker panels show how much of each run's summed intensity comes from skin (keratins), blood,
white cells, fat and muscle fibre. These shares describe the runs and decide nothing.

```{r}
#| label: contamination-index
qc_panels <- list(
  keratin = c(
    "KRT1", "KRT2", "KRT10", "KRT8", "KRT9", "KRT16", "KRT14", "KRT5", "KRT6A", "KRT6B", "DCD"
  ),
  blood = c(
    "HBB", "HBA1", "HBD", "HBG1", "HBG2", "HBQ1", "AHSP", "ALB", "CA1", "SLC4A1", "SPTA1"
  ),
  leukocyte = c("MPO", "CTSG", "ELANE", "PRTN3", "AZU1", "S100A8", "S100A9", "LYZ", "LTF"),
  adipose = c("FABP4", "PLIN1", "PLIN4", "ADIPOQ", "ADIRF"),
  myofibre = c(
    "MB", "CKM", "ACTA1", "MYH1", "MYH2", "MYH7", "ALDOA", "CASQ1", "PYGM", "ATP2A1", "DES"
  )
)
qc_index <- imap(qc_panels, \(genes, panel) {
  tibble(
    sample_id = colnames(intensity), panel = panel,
    pct_signal = 100 * colSums(intensity[annotation$gene %in% genes, , drop = FALSE],
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) / colSums(intensity, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  left_join(select(metadata, sample_id, subject, arm, timepoint), by = "sample_id")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-contamination
#| fig-cap: "Each run's signal share per contamination panel, before removal; filled HR, open LR."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5
qc_index |>
  filter(panel != "myofibre") |>
  ggplot(aes(timepoint, pct_signal, fill = timepoint)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.6, alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = arm), position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, seed = 42), size = 1.4) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Blues", guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(HR = 16, LR = 1), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% of run signal") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

## Contaminants, by identity

A protein is removed for what it is, never for how it behaves in these runs. Two sources say what
it is.

The curated list names 30 accessions in the code below (keratins and other skin proteins, globins,
immunoglobulin constant regions, complement) and 95 more in `references/blood_contaminants.csv`,
each with its class and reason (`references/README.md`). Matching is by accession only. Matching by
gene symbol or description fails here: the cRAP contaminant list's ALDOA_RABIT collides with muscle
ALDOA, and a trypsin or albumin pattern catches parvalbumin. Only cRAP's dust-and-contact section is
used, because its UPS1 standard section holds myoglobin and creatine kinase M, both muscle proteins.

```{r}
#| label: curated-list
contaminants <- tribble(
  ~uniprot_id, ~gene, ~class, ~reason,
  "P04264", "KRT1", "keratin", "cRAP dust/contact; cornified epidermal",
  "P35908", "KRT2", "keratin", "cRAP dust/contact; epidermal",
  "P13645", "KRT10", "keratin", "cRAP dust/contact; type-I partner of KRT1",
  "P35527", "KRT9", "keratin", "cRAP dust/contact; palmoplantar",
  "P08779", "KRT16", "keratin", "cRAP dust/contact",
  "P04259", "KRT6B", "keratin", "cRAP dust/contact",
  "P02533", "KRT14", "keratin", "cRAP dust/contact; basal epidermal",
  "P13647", "KRT5", "keratin", "cRAP dust/contact; basal epidermal",
  "P02538", "KRT6A", "keratin", "cRAP dust/contact",
  "Q04695", "KRT17", "keratin", "cRAP dust/contact",
  "Q7Z794", "KRT77", "keratin", "cRAP dust/contact",
  "Q8N1N4", "KRT78", "keratin", "cRAP dust/contact",
  "P05787", "KRT8", "keratin", "simple-epithelial; Spearman +0.78 with the KRT1/2/10 load",
  "P15924", "DSP", "keratin", "desmoplakin; skin desmosome",
  "Q02413", "DSG1", "keratin", "desmoglein-1; skin desmosome",
  "P81605", "DCD", "keratin", "dermcidin; sweat",
  "P31151", "S100A7", "keratin", "psoriasin; skin",
  "P01040", "CSTA", "keratin", "cystatin-A; cornified envelope",
  "P68871", "HBB", "globin", "red-cell carryover",
  "P69905", "HBA1", "globin", "red-cell carryover",
  "P02042", "HBD", "globin", "red-cell carryover",
  "P69891", "HBG1", "globin", "red-cell carryover",
  "P69892", "HBG2", "globin", "orphan gamma-globin; shares tryptic peptides with HBB/HBD",
  "P09105", "HBQ1", "globin", "red-cell carryover",
  "Q9NZD4", "AHSP", "globin", "erythroid-specific haemoglobin chaperone",
  "P01834", "IGKC", "immunoglobulin", "absent from HPA; constant region",
  "P01860", "IGHG3", "immunoglobulin", "absent from HPA; constant region",
  "P01880", "IGHD", "immunoglobulin", "absent from HPA; constant region",
  "P02746", "C1QB", "complement", "absent from HPA",
  "P00736", "C1R", "complement", "absent from HPA"
) |>
  bind_rows(
    read_csv(paths[["blood"]], col_types = cols(.default = "c")) |>
      select(uniprot_id, gene, class, reason)
  )
count(contaminants, class)
```

The Human Protein Atlas (HPA) tags proteins the list misses: secreted to blood (plasma), an
immunoglobulin gene, or erythrocyte RNA at or above 5,000 nCPM (normalised transcripts per million
in single-cell data). A blood-tagged protein is rescued as muscle when myonuclei express it at
20 nCPM or more and its plasma concentration is below 10^9 pg/L.

Evidence behind these cuts:

- `myo_cut` 20: at 50 the rescue missed GPI (43.1 nCPM), ANXA2 (40.2) and PPIA (21.1), all muscle
  proteins; the plasma-concentration cap, not this floor, separates plasma from muscle.
- `ery_cut` 5,000 and `blood_max` 10^9 pg/L: no recorded evidence. The V1 decisions log notes that
  mature red cells carry almost no RNA, so the erythrocyte RNA tag caught none of six known
  red-cell proteins there; the curated list carries that load instead.

Absence from HPA never removes a protein. Membership of the red-cell reference proteome (`in_rbc`,
five published red-cell proteomes) is reported and removes nothing, because red cells share much
of their proteome with muscle.

```{r}
#| label: hpa
strip_iso <- function(x) sub("-[0-9]+$", "", x)
hpa <- read_tsv(paths[["hpa"]], show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  transmute(
    acc = Uniprot, protein_class = `Protein class`, secretome = `Secretome location`,
    blood_conc = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(`Blood concentration - Conc. blood MS [pg/L]`)),
    ery = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(`Single Cell Type RNA - Erythrocytes [nCPM]`)),
    myo = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(`Single Cell Type RNA - Myonuclei [nCPM]`))
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(acc), acc != "") |>
  separate_longer_delim(acc, delim = ", ") |>
  mutate(acc = strip_iso(acc)) |>
  distinct(acc, .keep_all = TRUE)
rbc <- read_tsv(paths[["rbc"]], show_col_types = FALSE)
c(hpa_accessions = nrow(hpa), rbc_reference = nrow(rbc))
```

Each protein gets one verdict. The curated list wins first; then a blood tag removes unless the
muscle rescue applies.

```{r}
#| label: verdicts
protein_calls <- annotation |>
  mutate(acc = strip_iso(uniprot_id), blood_cor = blood_cor) |>
  left_join(hpa, by = "acc") |>
  left_join(
    select(contaminants, acc = uniprot_id, contam_class = class, contam_reason = reason),
    by = "acc"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    is_curated = !is.na(contam_class),
    is_ery = !is.na(ery) & ery >= 5000,
    is_ig = str_detect(coalesce(protein_class, ""), "Immunoglobulin genes"),
    is_plasma = !is.na(secretome) & secretome == "Secreted to blood",
    in_rbc = acc %in% na.omit(rbc$acc) | gene %in% na.omit(rbc$gene),
    rescued = !is.na(myo) & myo >= 20 & (is.na(blood_conc) | blood_conc < 1e9),
    is_blood = is_ery | is_ig | is_plasma,
    contaminant = is_curated | (is_blood & !rescued),
    verdict = case_when(
      is_curated ~ paste0("remove: ", contam_class),
      is_blood & rescued ~ "keep: rescued (muscle-expressed)",
      is_plasma ~ "remove: plasma",
      is_ig ~ "remove: immunoglobulin",
      is_ery ~ "remove: erythrocyte",
      TRUE ~ "keep"
    ),
    reason = coalesce(contam_reason, verdict)
  ) |>
  select(
    uniprot_id, gene, description, verdict, reason, contaminant, in_rbc,
    secretome, blood_conc, ery, myo, blood_cor
  )
stopifnot(protein_calls$contaminant == str_starts(protein_calls$verdict, "remove"))
count(protein_calls, verdict)
protein_calls |>
  filter(str_detect(verdict, "rescued")) |>
  slice_max(myo, n = 5) |>
  select(gene, secretome, blood_conc, myo)
```

The kept proteins enter a `DAList`. proteoDA's own annotation filter is not used: its class check
calls `if()` on a length-2 class vector and errors on every real `DAList` (package behaviour, seen
in V1), so the subset is plain indexing. `zero_to_missing()` then turns DIA-NN's zeros, which mean
"not detected", into `NA`.

```{r}
#| label: dalist
keep <- !protein_calls$contaminant
int_df <- as.data.frame(intensity[keep, ])
annot_df <- as.data.frame(annotation[keep, ])
rownames(int_df) <- rownames(annot_df) <- annot_df$uniprot_id
c(zeros_before = sum(int_df == 0, na.rm = TRUE), na_before = sum(is.na(int_df)))
dal <- zero_to_missing(DAList(data = int_df, annotation = annot_df, metadata = metadata))
c(zeros_after = sum(dal$data == 0, na.rm = TRUE), na_after = sum(is.na(dal$data)))
```

## Outlier runs

Four checks each flag runs that sit far from the rest:

- missingness: a run's share of missing values, or its gap from the same person's other runs,
  beyond the Tukey fence (upper quartile + 1.5 × interquartile range);
- PCA distance: Mahalanobis distance on the first three principal components of the proteins seen
  in every run, beyond the chi-square 0.99 quantile;
- median intensity: more than 3 median absolute deviations (MAD) from the median run (the Hampel
  rule);
- correlation: a run's median correlation with the other runs, more than 3 MAD below the median.

A run is removed when three of the four agree. Evidence (decisions log, 2026-10-06): kept, these
runs lowered limpa's detection-curve slope from 0.67 to 0.59, and limma's sample weights did not
single them out. The manuscript's pipeline removes the same three runs by its own consensus.

```{r}
#| label: outlier-flags
lg <- log2(dal$data + 1)
complete <- dal$data[rowSums(is.na(dal$data)) == 0, ]
pcs <- prcomp(t(log2(complete + 1)), center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)$x[, 1:3]
med_cor <- apply(cor(lg, use = "pairwise.complete.obs"), 2, \(x) median(x[x < 1], na.rm = TRUE))
hampel <- function(x) abs(x - median(x)) > 3 * mad(x)
tukey <- function(x) x > quantile(x, 0.75) + 1.5 * IQR(x)

outlier_diag <- dal$metadata |>
  select(sample_id, subject, arm, timepoint) |>
  mutate(
    pct_missing = colMeans(is.na(dal$data))[sample_id] * 100,
    delta_missing = ave(pct_missing, subject, FUN = \(x) pmax(x - min(x), max(x) - x)),
    miss_flag = tukey(pct_missing) | tukey(delta_missing),
    pca_flag = mahalanobis(pcs, colMeans(pcs), cov(pcs)) > qchisq(0.99, df = 3),
    mad_flag = hampel(apply(lg, 2, median, na.rm = TRUE)[sample_id]),
    cor_flag = med_cor[sample_id] < median(med_cor) - 3 * mad(med_cor),
    n_flags = miss_flag + pca_flag + mad_flag + cor_flag,
    consensus_outlier = n_flags >= 3
  )
stopifnot(identical(rownames(pcs), outlier_diag$sample_id))
outlier_ids <- outlier_diag$sample_id[outlier_diag$consensus_outlier]
outlier_diag |>
  filter(n_flags > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(n_flags)) |>
  select(sample_id, ends_with("_flag"), n_flags)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-outliers
#| fig-cap: "Runs flagged by at least one outlier check. Three or more flags remove a run."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3.5
outlier_diag |>
  filter(n_flags > 0) |>
  pivot_longer(ends_with("_flag"), names_to = "method", values_to = "flagged") |>
  mutate(sample_id = fct_reorder(sample_id, n_flags)) |>
  ggplot(aes(method, sample_id, fill = flagged)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#D6604D", `FALSE` = "grey92"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

```{r}
#| label: drop-outliers
dal <- filter_samples(dal, !(sample_id %in% outlier_ids))
c(runs_removed = length(outlier_ids), runs_kept = ncol(dal$data))
```

## Detection filter

`filter_proteins_by_group()` (proteoDA) keeps a protein detected in at least `min_reps` runs of
at least `min_groups` of the six group-by-time cells. Here a protein needs 5 detections in one
cell. This is the one step in 01_Processing that reads the HR/LR label; it counts detections and
never compares abundance. It runs after the outlier removal so that no discarded run counts toward
a detection. The floor of 5 has no recorded evidence beyond being a majority of a cell of 7 or 8.

```{r}
#| label: detection
n_before <- nrow(dal$data)
dal <- filter_proteins_by_group(dal, min_reps = 5, min_groups = 1, grouping_column = "group")
c(before = n_before, after = nrow(dal$data))
```

## Blood by arm at T3

If one arm's T3 biopsies carried more blood, the acute interaction contrasts would partly measure
blood. A mixed model (arm × timepoint, a random intercept per person, fitted with lme4) estimates
the LR-minus-HR difference at T3 on two scales: the log2 blood index and the blood panel's share of
signal. The permutation p shuffles the arm label across people 999 times and asks how often a
shuffled t is at least as large as the observed one.

```{r}
#| label: blood-by-arm
blood_data <- dal$metadata |>
  select(sample_id, subject, arm, timepoint) |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, c("HR", "LR")), log2_index = unname(blood_index[sample_id])) |>
  left_join(filter(qc_index, panel == "blood") |> select(sample_id, pct_signal), by = "sample_id")
arm_by_t3 <- function(data, response) {
  fit <- suppressMessages(lme4::lmer(
    reformulate(c("arm * timepoint", "(1 | subject)"), response),
    data = data
  ))
  coef(summary(fit))["armLR:timepointT3", c("Estimate", "t value")]
}
set.seed(42)
arms <- distinct(blood_data, subject, arm)
blood_by_arm <- map(set_names(c("log2_index", "pct_signal")), \(response) {
  observed <- arm_by_t3(blood_data, response)
  null_t <- replicate(999, {
    shuffled <- set_names(sample(arms$arm), arms$subject)
    arm_by_t3(mutate(blood_data, arm = shuffled[subject]), response)[["t value"]]
  })
  tibble(
    scale = response, lr_minus_hr_at_t3 = round(observed[["Estimate"]], 3),
    t = round(observed[["t value"]], 2),
    permutation_p = permutation_p(abs(observed[["t value"]]), abs(null_t))
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind()
blood_by_arm
```

## Why no single blood_cor cut

How large a chance correlation with the blood index can be depends on how many runs saw the
protein. Shuffling the index 300 times and taking the 99.9th percentile of |rho| by observation
count shows that no single cut serves every protein, which is why `blood_cor` removes nothing.

```{r}
#| label: blood-cor-null
set.seed(42)
tested <- log_int[testable, ]
blood_null_rho <- replicate(300, abs(as.vector(suppressWarnings(cor(
  t(tested), sample(blood_index),
  method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs"
)))))
n_obs <- cut(rowSums(!is.na(tested)), c(0, 25, 40, Inf), c("15-25", "26-40", "41-48"))
null_999 <- \(rows) round(quantile(blood_null_rho[rows, ], 0.999, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE), 3)
blood_null <- bind_rows(
  map(levels(n_obs), \(bin) {
    tibble(observations = bin, proteins = sum(n_obs == bin), null_999 = null_999(n_obs == bin))
  }),
  tibble(observations = "all", proteins = length(n_obs), null_999 = null_999(TRUE))
)
blood_null
```

## Validation

The filtered object must hold only kept proteins and runs, with the sample sheet still aligned to
the data columns and no contaminant left.

```{r}
#| label: validate
stopifnot(
  identical(colnames(dal$data), dal$metadata$sample_id),
  identical(rownames(dal$data), dal$annotation$uniprot_id),
  !any(rownames(dal$data) %in% protein_calls$uniprot_id[protein_calls$contaminant]),
  !any(colnames(dal$data) %in% outlier_ids),
  !anyNA(dal$metadata$blood_rel)
)
```

## Summary

```{r}
#| label: filter-log
removed <- count(filter(protein_calls, contaminant), verdict, name = "n_removed")
filter_log <- tibble(
  step = c("raw input", "duplicate accession", removed$verdict, "outlier samples", "detection"),
  n_removed = c(NA, n_raw - n_dedup, removed$n_removed, 0L, n_before - nrow(dal$data))
) |>
  mutate(
    n_after = n_raw - cumsum(coalesce(n_removed, 0L)),
    pct_of_raw = round(100 * n_after / n_raw, 1),
    n_samples = c(rep(nrow(metadata), nrow(removed) + 2), rep(ncol(dal$data), 2))
  )
filter_log
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-cascade
#| fig-cap: "Proteins removed at each filtering step, and the number left after it."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
filter_log |>
  filter(!is.na(n_removed)) |>
  mutate(step = fct_inorder(str_remove(step, "^remove: ")), ymax = n_after + n_removed) |>
  ggplot(aes(step)) +
  geom_rect(aes(
    xmin = as.numeric(step) - 0.35, xmax = as.numeric(step) + 0.35, ymin = n_after, ymax = ymax
  ), fill = "#D6604D") +
  geom_step(aes(y = n_after, group = 1), direction = "mid", colour = "grey35") +
  geom_text(aes(y = ymax, label = if_else(n_removed > 0, paste0("-", n_removed), "")),
    vjust = -0.6, size = 3, colour = "#B2182B"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "proteins retained") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1))
```

`r n_raw` proteins were measured in `r nrow(metadata)` runs.
`r sum(protein_calls$contaminant)` went as contaminants and `r n_before - nrow(dal$data)` by the
detection filter, leaving `r nrow(dal$data)` proteins. `r length(outlier_ids)` runs
(`r paste(outlier_ids, collapse = ", ")`) failed three or more outlier checks, leaving
`r ncol(dal$data)`.

## Save

`DAList_filtered.rds` is the input to normalisation. The workbook keeps every table above;
`01_Processing/Figures/S01_QC` reads it.

```{r}
#| label: save
saveRDS(dal, file.path(out, "DAList_filtered.rds"), compress = "xz")
sheets <- list(
  filter_log = filter_log,
  contaminants_removed = arrange(filter(protein_calls, contaminant), verdict, gene),
  rescued = arrange(filter(protein_calls, str_detect(verdict, "rescued")), desc(myo)),
  protein_calls = protein_calls,
  contamination_index = qc_index,
  blood_index = tibble(
    sample_id = names(blood_index), blood_index = unname(blood_index),
    blood_rel = unname(blood_rel)
  ),
  outlier_diagnostics = outlier_diag,
  blood_by_arm = blood_by_arm,
  blood_cor_null = blood_null
)
holds <- c(
  "Proteins left after each step.",
  "Every protein removed as a contaminant, with its verdict and reason.",
  "Blood-tagged proteins kept by the muscle rescue.",
  "One verdict per protein, with the annotation behind it.",
  "Share of each sample's signal per contamination panel, before removal.",
  "Mean log2 haemoglobin per sample, raw and relative to the sample's median log2 intensity.",
  "The four outlier flags per sample.",
  "Arm by T3 blood term on two scales, with a permutation p.",
  "99.9th percentile of the blood_cor permutation null, by observation count."
)
write_workbook(sheets, holds, file.path(out, "protein_filtering.xlsx"), inputs, paths)
```
